title: Header and Source File Separation
learningObjectives: Explain header and source file separation.
Identify the function's role, inputs and control flow.
Trace calls, local state and returned results.
Recognize common design or safety mistakes.
Write and test a reusable function for a practical task.

understand.concept: A header file commonly contains declarations, types and interface information. A source file contains definitions. Include guards or pragma once prevent the same header from being processed repeatedly within one translation unit.
understand.whyItMatters: Separating interface and implementation supports reuse, multiple source files, clearer dependencies and more maintainable compilation.
understand.explain: Include the header in its implementation file so the compiler checks that declarations match. Avoid defining non-inline functions in headers that are included by multiple source files, which can create duplicate definitions.

practise.guidedTask: Walk through all five Header and Source File Separation examples. Annotate the signature, call arguments, local state, control flow, return behavior and side effects.
practise.independentTask: Create a header and source file for a small math helper library, then use the header in main. Explain declarations, definitions, include protection and the role of linking.
hints: Start with the function signature and intended contract.
Trace each call with a small input.
Separate calculation from output when appropriate.
Test normal, boundary and invalid cases.
Check lifetimes, side effects and termination.
